full_judgment: 3. The relevant facts as stated in that writ petition were that one A. K. M. Abdur Rahman was allotted the land in question appertaining to plot No.7, Road No.10, Block-C, Section-6, Mirpur Housing Estate, Dhaka on 01.11.1963. Subsequently the heirs of the said allottee transferred the said land and the structure thereon in favour of Mrs. Sitara Arshad and Mrs. Rahena Pathan by registered kabala dated 01.02.1987. Those two purchasers subsequently transferred the said land along with the structure to the petitioners by kabala dated 01.12.2006. That the petitioners. thereafter came to know that the said property was illegally included in the list of abandoned property and as such they prayed to the court of settlement on 28.03.2007 for getting the said land released from the list of abandoned property, but the said prayer was rejected by the court of settlement on point of limitation by the order dated 02.03.2007. Thereafter the petitioners preferred the writ petition challenging the enlistment of the property in question in the list of abandoned property and obtained rule. A Division Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing both the parties, discharged that rule by the impugned judgment and order making observations to the effect that the writ petitioners had failed to produce a single piece of document in support of physical possession of the original allottee in the property in question since 1971 and that alleged transfer deeds dated 01.02.1987 and 01.12.2006 in respect of the property in question were created illegally for the purpose of grabbing the property in question.
